project.name: GDBM
project.commit_note: The metadata does not provide a vulnerable commit hash; this GT is grounded in the exact staged vulnerable source snapshot under `gt_results/arvo_38943/_work/src/gdbm` that produced the saved Stage 01 crash.

classification.classification_note: The project-side defect is an unchecked out-of-bounds read from the in-memory directory array during sequential key verification.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in sequential access where key verification is not properly performed. In src/gdbmseq.c, the function gdbm_valid_key_p does not use gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p to validate the buffer index, and the order of checks is incorrect. This can lead to improper validation of keys during sequential access.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 1511-byte witness is a malformed GDBM database image consumed through the fixed `gdbm_fuzzer.rc` command script, which executes `open` and then the sequential-access command `first`. During `open`, `gdbm_fd_open` reads a 64-bit numsync header whose attacker-controlled fields encode `dir_size = 262` and `dir_bits = 6`; `validate_header` accepts that combination, and the header is copied into `dbf->header` and used to size the in-memory directory. On `first`, `_gdbm_get_bucket` safely validates and loads the current bucket at directory slot 0, `get_next_key` reads the first on-disk key from that bucket, and `gdbm_valid_key_p` rehashes the key with `_gdbm_hash_key`. Because the admitted header keeps `dir_bits = 6`, the recomputed directory index can exceed `GDBM_DIR_COUNT(dbf)`, which is only 32 for the witness header. The witness entry's stored hash matches the recomputed hash, so the buggy condition continues to `dbf->dir[bucket] == dbf->dir[dbf->bucket_dir]` without first checking `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p (dbf, bucket)`. That unchecked directory lookup reads past the 32-entry directory array, and Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ` at `src/gdbmseq.c:34:7` in `gdbm_valid_key_p`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled database bytes and materializes the vulnerability-relevant header state.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is the exact 1511-byte database image written verbatim by the harness before the fixed `gdbm_fuzzer.rc` script runs `open`. Its first 32 bytes are `d1 9a 57 13 fd 00 00 00 04 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 06 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 06 00 00 00`: `d1 9a 57 13` is `GDBM_NUMSYNC_MAGIC64`, so this read materializes a 64-bit header with `dir_size = 262`, `dir_bits = 6`, `bucket_size = 262`, and `bucket_elems = 6` from attacker-controlled bytes.

sink.description: ASan crash site: the recomputed bucket is used as an unchecked directory index, producing the out-of-bounds read.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/gdbmseq.c:34:7` in this comparison, with project frames `get_next_key -> gdbm_firstkey -> firstkey_handler` beneath the top frame.

root_cause.description: Sequential key verification dereferences `dbf->dir[bucket]` without first validating that the recomputed bucket is a legal directory index.
root_cause.note: The fix exports `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p` and inserts `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p (dbf, bucket)` as the first conjunct before any `dbf->dir[bucket]` access. In the vulnerable source, the condition above performs the directory lookup as soon as the hash-equality conjunct succeeds.

tainted_value_origin.description: The unchecked directory index is derived here from attacker-controlled key bytes together with the admitted header's `dbf->header->dir_bits`.

parser_admitted.description: The malformed database passes the header-admission gate and is accepted as an opened GDBM file.
parser_admitted.condition: For the witness header, `validate_header` accepts `block_size = 253`, `dir_size = 262`, and `dir_bits = 6` because `dir_size` is at least the minimum computed from `block_size` and `compute_directory_size(262)` reproduces `dir_bits = 6`, so the `open` command reaches the sequential-access path instead of failing early.

coarse_trace.summary: The `open` command reads the attacker-controlled GDBM header and directory, admits a header with `dir_size = 262` and `dir_bits = 6`, and stores that geometry in `dbf->header` and `dbf->dir`.
Sequential access begins by validating and loading the current bucket for directory slot 0, establishing `dbf->bucket_dir` and the current bucket metadata used for key verification.
The first non-empty bucket element is read from disk, and its key bytes are passed into `gdbm_valid_key_p` for rehash-based bucket verification.

The verifier rehashes the on-disk key to a bucket outside the 32-entry directory, confirms the hash matches the bucket element, and then dereferences `dbf->dir[bucket]` without `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p`, triggering the ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `gdbm_fd_open` reads the attacker-controlled database header into `partial_header`. For the witness bytes, this materializes a 64-bit numsync header whose relevant fields are `dir_size = 262`, `dir_bits = 6`, `bucket_size = 262`, and `bucket_elems = 6`.

The malformed header is admitted. `validate_header` only requires `dir_size` to be at least the minimum for `block_size` and `compute_directory_size (262)` to reproduce `dir_bits = 6`, so this witness reaches the open-success path instead of being rejected.

The admitted header becomes persistent database state. From this point `dbf->header->dir_bits` is 6, while `GDBM_DIR_COUNT (dbf)` derived from the same header will expose only 32 logical directory entries for the witness.

The directory array is materialized from attacker-controlled bytes using the admitted header geometry. `dbf->dir` was allocated with `dbf->header->dir_size` bytes just above, and for this witness `GDBM_DIR_COUNT (dbf)` is 32, so later directory lookups must stay in indices 0..31.

When sequential access starts with `gdbm_firstkey`, `_gdbm_get_bucket` validates the current directory index before touching `dbf->dir[dir_index]`, then stores `dbf->bucket_dir = 0` and resolves the current bucket from `dbf->dir[0]`. This guarded current-bucket state is what the later verifier compares against.

For the first non-empty bucket element selected by `get_next_key`, `_gdbm_read_entry` reads the on-disk key/data record into the cache buffer. The first `key_size` bytes of `data_ca->dptr` become the `find_data`/`key_ptr` buffer passed into `gdbm_valid_key_p`.

The sequential verifier materializes a `datum key` from the on-disk key bytes read in step 6 and the selected bucket element's stored `key_size`, preserving the exact attacker-controlled key that will be rehashed.

The verifier rehashes the attacker-controlled key and derives the directory index `bucket` from `dbf->header->dir_bits`. With the admitted witness header, `_gdbm_bucket_dir` uses 6 top hash bits, so any out-of-range result must lie in 32..63; the reproduced crash proves this witness key hashes into that invalid range.

The first conjunct succeeds for the witness entry. Because `&&` short-circuits left-to-right, this successful hash comparison is what makes evaluation continue to the directory-comparison half of the condition on the next line.

Root cause. Unlike `_gdbm_get_bucket`, this verifier does not require `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p (dbf, bucket)` before reusing the recomputed `bucket` as a directory index. Once step 9 makes the first conjunct true, the vulnerable code proceeds toward a directory lookup on a bucket that is already outside the 32-entry directory extent.

Sink. The second conjunct dereferences the out-of-range `bucket` against the in-memory directory array while comparing it to the current bucket's address at `dbf->dir[dbf->bucket_dir]`. AddressSanitizer reports this exact read as a heap-buffer-overflow at `src/gdbmseq.c:34:7`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch exports `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p` and adds `gdbm_dir_entry_valid_p (dbf, bucket)` before any `dbf->dir[bucket]` read in `gdbm_valid_key_p`, which addresses the traced root cause. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `patch_resolves` remains false.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source under `gt_results/arvo_38943/_work/src/gdbm`, the staged patch.diff, the staged witness `poc`, and the fixed `fuzz/gdbm_fuzzer.rc` command script from the vulnerable snapshot

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved ASan crash location is `gdbm_valid_key_p` at `src/gdbmseq.c:34:7`, which is the same directory-read expression named by the top-level sink.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_38943 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ` in `gdbm_valid_key_p` at `src/gdbmseq.c:34:7`, with project stack `get_next_key -> gdbm_firstkey -> firstkey_handler`.

format.name: 1511-byte malformed GDBM database witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 1511-byte binary file `poc` (sha256 `7fa306c415ec34dd4875ed0403cd78f9b440b2a50125968439d663375fd20a7c`). Its opening bytes `d1 9a 57 13 fd 00 00 00 04 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 06 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 06 00 00 00` encode a 64-bit numsync GDBM header with `block_size = 253`, `dir = 0x204`, `dir_size = 262`, `dir_bits = 6`, `bucket_size = 262`, and `bucket_elems = 6`. The fixed command stream in the staged `fuzz/gdbm_fuzzer.rc` then executes `open` and later `first`, which drives sequential access into `gdbm_valid_key_p` on that admitted database image. This GT is grounded only for that exact witness file and command script, not for a generalized class of malformed GDBM databases.

evidence_limitations: The saved Stage 01 artifacts prove that the recomputed `bucket` was outside the valid directory range and that the hash-equality conjunct succeeded, but they do not expose the exact integer value of `bucket`; this trace therefore grounds the invalid range (`bucket >= GDBM_DIR_COUNT (dbf)`, here 32..63) rather than guessing a concrete index.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image. Patch grounding is therefore source- and diff-based only, not confirmed by a saved fixed-run trace.
